images.caption:
Ash Cave, Ohio.
"Ash Cave, spring 1937" typed on the envelope that I found with only this one negative.  I I found the cars in this view interesting. The next time I get over to the Hocking Hills, I'll see if the sign is still there and maybe photograph some of todays cars.

I recognize the 1931 Model A Ford at the left and the Chevrolet tail light on the pickup. Maybe someone will identify the other vehicles.

images.caption: Cedar Falls forms the head of Queer Creek Gorge in the scenic Hocking Hills of southeastern Ohio.  Most of the falls is a cascade, but terminates in a drop.  The cascade portion splits around a promontory.  The rocks are sandstones to pebbly sandstones of the Lower Mississippian Black Hand Sandstone, traditionally interpreted as an ancient delta deposit.  Modern work has shown it is an incised valley fill complex.

images.filename: Ash Cave Falls (Hocking Hills, Ohio, USA) 3 (34766042151).jpg
images.caption:
Ash Cave Falls in the scenic Hocking Hills of southeastern Ohio consists of a single drop of about 90 feet.  It starts at the rim of an overhanging cliff (rock shelter, or "recess cave") called Ash Cave.

The rocks are part of the Lower Mississippian Black Hand Sandstone.  The unit consists of quartzose sandstones and pebbly sandstones.  It was traditionally interpreted as an ancient delta deposit, but modern work has shown it is an incised valley fill complex.
